definitions.explanation: Substances added to food to enhance or modify its flavor, such as salt, soy sauce, or sugar.

examples.japanese: {基本|きほん}の{調味料|ちょうみりょう}は「さしすせそ」です。
examples.notes: Mnemonic for sugar, salt, vinegar, soy sauce, miso

examples.japanese: {調味料|ちょうみりょう}を{加|くわ}えて{味|あじ}を{調|ととの}える。
examples.english: Add seasonings to adjust the taste.

examples.japanese: {調味料|ちょうみりょう}の{入|い}れすぎに{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
examples.english: Be careful not to add too much seasoning.

notes:
The traditional Japanese seasoning order 「さしすせそ」:
- さ = {砂糖|さとう} (sugar) - add first
- し = {塩|しお} (salt)
- す = {酢|す} (vinegar)
- せ = {醤油|しょうゆ} (soy sauce)
- そ = {味噌|みそ} (miso) - add last

This order is based on molecule size and how flavors penetrate food. Sugar's larger molecules need more time to absorb.

Other common 調味料: みりん, {料理酒|りょうりしゅ}, だしの{素|もと}, ソース, マヨネーズ.
